_comment: Tier-2 for skfem hyperelasticity#9, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 / numpy 1.26.4. Claim: numpy's @ does not work on skfem (d,d,n_elem,n_quad) tensor fields; it tries the last-two-dims convention and aborts with 'matmul: Input operand 1 has a mismatch in its core dimension 0, with gufunc signature (n?,k),(k,m?)->(n?,m?)'. Ran: A @ B on a (2,2,8,3) field, then on a (2,2,3,3) field, then einsum and skfem.helpers.mul on the same data. Printed: the (2,2,8,3) case raises ValueError with the quoted prefix verbatim (concrete tail '(size 8 is different from 3)' -- numpy contracted over the ELEMENT and QUADRATURE axes, not the tensor indices). NEW AND MORE DANGEROUS: when n_elem == n_quad the shapes are conformable and @ raises NOTHING -- it returns a right-shaped (2,2,3,3) array whose entries deviate from the true tensor product by 1.5e+01, i.e. a silent wrong contraction. helpers.mul and einsum both reproduce the true product to 0.000e+00. Fixture asserts both branches so the silent one cannot regress unnoticed.
